quickAnswer: Türkiye's Digital Nomad Visa is open in 2026 to remote workers aged 21–55 from 36 eligible countries who hold a university degree and earn at least $3,000 per month ($36,000 annually) from outside Türkiye. Applicants complete an online pre-application for a Digital Nomad Identification Certificate, apply at a Turkish consulate, and then file for an İkamet inside Türkiye.

body.text: Which nationalities and age brackets qualify for Türkiye's Digital Nomad Visa?

The turkey digital nomad visa 2026 program is open strictly to citizens aged 21 to 55 from 36 designated countries, per the official [GoTürkiye Digital Nomad platform](https://goturkiye.com/digitalnomads/application-requirements-for-digital-nomad-visa-and-short-term-residence). Applicants must also hold a university diploma and a passport valid for at least six months beyond arrival.

Eligible nationalities cover every EU member state except Cyprus (Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Croatia, Czech Republic, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Italy, Latvia, Lithuania, Luxembourg, Malta, Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden), plus 10 non-EU countries: Belarus, Canada, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Russian Federation, Switzerland, Ukraine, the United Kingdom, and the United States. Citizens outside this list must check standard short-term residence options with a Turkish consulate or licensed immigration lawyer.
What monthly income threshold ($3,000+) and remote-work proof are required?

Applicants must prove steady foreign-sourced income of at least $3,000 USD per month or $36,000 USD per year, earned strictly from an employer, business, or clients outside Türkiye ([GoTürkiye Application Requirements](https://goturkiye.com/digitalnomads/application-requirements-for-digital-nomad-visa-and-short-term-residence)). Working for Turkish companies or invoicing domestic Turkish clients is prohibited under this status.
Prepare four core documents before uploading your pre-application:

items: Remote Work Proof: An employment contract with a non-Turkish company confirming remote work, or active client contracts and business registration for freelancers.
Income Evidence: Recent bank statements (typically 3–6 months, depending on the consulate) showing recurring monthly deposits averaging at least $3,000 USD, plus payslips or tax returns.
University Degree: Official higher-education diploma matching your passport name.
Passport & Photo: Valid passport scan (6+ months remaining) and biometric photograph.

body.text: How does the online pre-application connect to consulate and Ikamet steps?

Receiving the online certificate from digitalnomads.goturkiye.com is only Stage 1 of a three-step sequence—it is not a visa and does not grant legal entry or residency. You must attend a Turkish consulate or visa center abroad, enter Türkiye on the visa, and then file for a residence permit (İkamet).

How do tax residency (183-day rule) and phone registration apply?

Two compliance rules catch long-stay remote workers off guard: Turkish tax residency after six months and Türkiye's mobile phone IMEI tax after 120 days. Under Articles 3–6 of Income Tax Law No. 193 ([Turkish Revenue Administration](https://gib.gov.tr/)), staying over six months (183 days) in a calendar year generally triggers full tax residency.

Statutory temporary-stay exceptions and Double Taxation Treaties can modify that outcome ([2026 Turkish Tax Residency Guide](https://halilbakirci.av.tr/en/turkey-tax-residency-foreigners-six-month-rule-articles-3-6/)).
Consult a licensed Turkish CPA (SMMM) or tax lawyer before crossing 183 days to assess treaty tie-breakers and any applicable foreign-income exemptions.

For mobile devices, foreign-bought phones work on Turkish SIMs for 120 days per IMEI slot (resetting 1 January) before BTK blocks network access. From 1 January 2026, the statutory IMEI registration fee is TRY 54,258 (~$1,100–$1,263), filed solely via e-Devlet, limited to one phone every three calendar years, and locked to your own SIM ([2026 IMEI Guide](https://bayraktarattys.com/comprehensive-guide-to-registering-imported-phones-in-turkey); [Türkiye Today](https://www.turkiyetoday.com/business/turkiye-sets-2026-imei-registration-fee-for-phones-brought-from-abroad-at-1263-3212215)). Most 6-to-12-month nomads use a roaming eSIM, dual-SIM slot split, or an inexpensive locally bought hotspot phone instead.

faq.q: Can I apply for Türkiye's Digital Nomad Visa while already inside Türkiye?
faq.a: No. Stage 2 requires submitting your Digital Nomad Identification Certificate in person at a Turkish consulate or authorized visa center outside Türkiye.

faq.q: Does the Digital Nomad Visa cover my spouse or children?
faq.a: The certificate covers the individual remote worker. Accompanying spouses or children typically require separate visa and residence permit filings confirmed with a consulate or immigration lawyer.

faq.q: Can freelancers with multiple clients qualify for the $3,000 threshold?
faq.a: Yes, provided client contracts, business registration records, and bank statements prove at least $3,000/month or $36,000/year from outside Türkiye.

faq.q: Do I need to pay the TRY 54,258 phone tax if I stay under four months?
faq.a: No. Foreign phones work on Turkish SIMs for up to 120 days per IMEI slot without registration, and international roaming eSIMs do not trigger the domestic 120-day timer.

faq.q: Is private health insurance required for the Digital Nomad Ikamet step?
faq.a: Yes. Stage 3 (İkamet) inside Türkiye requires a compliant Turkish residence health insurance policy covering your full permit duration.

faq.q: Does a Digital Nomad Visa exempt me from Turkish income tax automatically?
faq.a: No. Tax residency is governed by Income Tax Law No. 193 and Double Taxation Treaties; obtain formal advice from a licensed Turkish tax advisor before exceeding 183 days.
